comment: Biology multiple choice for module 02. Four options, answer is the 0-based index of the correct one.

02-photosynthesis.q: Which is the word equation for photosynthesis?
02-photosynthesis.explain: Carbon dioxide and water are the reactants; glucose and oxygen the products. The first option is respiration.

02-photosynthesis.q: Which is the balanced symbol equation for photosynthesis?
02-photosynthesis.explain: Six of each small molecule balance one glucose. The last option is respiration.

02-photosynthesis.q: Where in a plant cell does photosynthesis take place?
02-photosynthesis.explain: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll. Mitochondria are for respiration.

02-photosynthesis.q: What is the job of chlorophyll?
02-photosynthesis.explain: Chlorophyll is the green pigment that absorbs light.

02-photosynthesis.q: Which element is needed to make chlorophyll?
02-photosynthesis.explain: Magnesium ions are needed for chlorophyll; without them leaves turn yellow.

02-photosynthesis.q: In photosynthesis, light energy is converted into…
02-photosynthesis.explain: The energy is stored as chemical energy in glucose.

02-photosynthesis.q: Photosynthesis is described as endothermic because it…
02-photosynthesis.explain: It takes in light energy from the surroundings.

02-photosynthesis.q: Which structure is found in plant cells but NOT animal cells?
02-photosynthesis.explain: Cell wall, chloroplasts and permanent vacuole are plant-only.

02-photosynthesis.q: What is a plant cell wall made of?
02-photosynthesis.explain: Cellulose, made from glucose.

02-photosynthesis.q: Why do plants store glucose as starch?
options: Starch is insoluble so it does not affect osmosis
02-photosynthesis.explain: Insoluble starch does not draw water into cells by osmosis.

02-photosynthesis.q: In what form is sugar transported in the phloem?
02-photosynthesis.explain: Sucrose is the transport sugar.

02-photosynthesis.q: Plants need nitrate ions to make…
02-photosynthesis.explain: Nitrate supplies the nitrogen in amino acids.

02-photosynthesis.q: A limiting factor is…
options: the factor in shortest supply that limits the rate
any factor that kills the plant
02-photosynthesis.explain: Whatever is in shortest supply holds the rate back.

02-photosynthesis.q: Which is NOT a limiting factor of photosynthesis?
02-photosynthesis.explain: Oxygen is a product, not one of the three limiting factors.

02-photosynthesis.q: On a graph of rate against light intensity, the line levels off. This is because…
options: another factor, such as CO₂ concentration, is now limiting
02-photosynthesis.explain: Light is no longer limiting — name another factor.

02-photosynthesis.q: Where the rate rises with light intensity, the limiting factor is…
02-photosynthesis.explain: If more light gives a faster rate, light was limiting.

02-photosynthesis.q: Why does the rate of photosynthesis fall at very high temperatures?
02-photosynthesis.explain: The active sites of the enzymes change shape.

02-photosynthesis.q: A lamp is moved from 10 cm to 20 cm from a plant. The light intensity becomes…
02-photosynthesis.explain: Inverse square law: 1 ÷ 2² = 1/4.

02-photosynthesis.q: A lamp is moved from 10 cm to 30 cm. The light intensity becomes…
Which layer of the leaf contains the most chloroplasts?
02-photosynthesis.explain: Palisade cells are packed with chloroplasts near the top of the leaf.

02-photosynthesis.q: What is the function of the air spaces in the spongy mesophyll?
options: To give a large surface area for gas exchange
02-photosynthesis.explain: Gases diffuse through the air spaces into the cells.

02-photosynthesis.q: What controls the opening and closing of stomata?
02-photosynthesis.explain: A pair of guard cells surrounds each stoma.

02-photosynthesis.q: Why is the waxy cuticle important?
02-photosynthesis.explain: It is waterproof; it is also transparent.

02-photosynthesis.q: Why are leaves thin?
02-photosynthesis.explain: Gases only have to diffuse a short way.

02-photosynthesis.q: Closing the stomata reduces photosynthesis because…
02-photosynthesis.explain: CO₂ enters through the stomata.

02-photosynthesis.q: Transpiration is…
options: the uptake of water by roots
the loss of water vapour from the leaves
the movement of sugar in the phloem
02-photosynthesis.explain: Water evaporates and diffuses out through the stomata.

02-photosynthesis.q: Water enters root hair cells by…
02-photosynthesis.explain: Water moves by osmosis; mineral ions often by active transport.

02-photosynthesis.q: Which vessels carry water up the plant?
02-photosynthesis.explain: Xylem carries water and minerals upwards.

02-photosynthesis.q: Which condition would slow down transpiration?
02-photosynthesis.explain: Humid air means a smaller concentration gradient for water vapour.

02-photosynthesis.q: In the dark, a plant…
options: respires, so there is a net release of CO₂
02-photosynthesis.explain: Respiration never stops.

02-photosynthesis.q: At the compensation point…
options: the rate of photosynthesis equals the rate of respiration
02-photosynthesis.explain: There is no net gas exchange.

02-photosynthesis.q: In bright light there is a net uptake of CO₂ because…
02-photosynthesis.explain: The plant still respires; photosynthesis uses CO₂ faster.

02-photosynthesis.q: Hydrogencarbonate indicator turns yellow when carbon dioxide…
02-photosynthesis.explain: Yellow = high CO₂; purple = low CO₂.

02-photosynthesis.q: A leaf in bright light in hydrogencarbonate indicator turns it…
02-photosynthesis.explain: Photosynthesis removes CO₂, so the indicator turns purple.

02-photosynthesis.q: In the pondweed experiment, why is sodium hydrogencarbonate added to the water?
02-photosynthesis.explain: It releases CO₂, so CO₂ is not limiting.

02-photosynthesis.q: In the pondweed experiment, the bubbles given off are…
02-photosynthesis.explain: Oxygen is a product of photosynthesis.

02-photosynthesis.q: Why is a plant destarched before a starch test experiment?
options: So any starch found was made during the experiment
02-photosynthesis.explain: Old starch would give a false positive.

02-photosynthesis.q: Why is a leaf boiled in ethanol in the starch test?
02-photosynthesis.explain: Removing the green makes the iodine colour visible.

02-photosynthesis.q: Iodine turns blue-black in the presence of…
02-photosynthesis.explain: Iodine is orange-brown; blue-black shows starch.

02-photosynthesis.q: A variegated leaf is used to show that photosynthesis needs…
02-photosynthesis.explain: Only the green parts, with chlorophyll, make starch.
